memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "and worked them ruthlessly. They made their lives bitter with harsh labour in brick and mortar and with all kinds of work in the fields; in all their harsh labour the Egyptians worked them ruthlessly." - Exodus 1:13-14 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Read these two verses slowly and notice how the word ruthlessly appears twice, wrapping the sentence like a chain. The writer wants us to feel the weight. This was not inconvenience. It was bitterness in brick and mortar, day after day, with no end in sight.

Scripture does not rush past suffering. It does not tell Israel to be positive or to count their blessings. It simply records the bitterness honestly, because God is not embarrassed by our pain.

If your life feels bitter right now — a marriage that has become hard labour, a job that drains you, an illness that has stolen your energy — you are allowed to say so before God. The Psalms are full of such honesty. Faith is not pretending things are fine.

And remember this: God saw every brick. In the next chapter we will read that He heard, He remembered, He saw, He was concerned. Their deliverance was already being prepared while they were still in the mud. The One who later cried out on a cross knows exactly what bitterness feels like (Heb 4:15).

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Have I been honest with God about what is hardest right now?
2. Do I believe God sees my situation even when nothing changes?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, You know how heavy this season is. I bring You my tiredness without pretending. Please see me, and hold me until You bring relief. Amen.
